newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA NEEDS TO IMPORT 75,000T WHEAT - MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA NEEDS TO IMPORT 75,000T WHEAT - MINISTER.

text.p: Bulgaria needs to import 75,000 tonnes of wheat to cover the gap until the new crop, interim agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said on Tuesday.

"The interim government has partly solved the grains crisis in the country but the new government will have to import some 75,000 tonnes to cover the gap until the new harvest," he told a news conference.
Swiss firm Glencore was awarded two tenders in March and May to import a total of 100,000 tonnes of wheat in return for 131,750 tonnes of exports from this year's crop.
Bulgaria received 100,000 tonnes of wheat from Poland in March against an agreement to export the same quantity from the new crop.
"The interim government has agreed a draft bill to secure a minimum farm gate price set at 80 percent of international prices to stimulate the local producers," Hristov said.

Agriculture experts say the new crop, which is expected to be much better than last year's, will enable Bulgaria to meet its domestic needs, service export commitments under forward contracts and put aside wheat for the State Reserve.

Hristov said earlier this month the interim cabinet would not import U.S. bread wheat under the U.S. Department of Agriculture's GSM-102 export credit guarantee programme as the price of more than $210 per tonne was too high.
He said negotiations would be held with Hungary, as the price would be $190 and delivery time would be much shorter.
Hristov is to be replaced by Ventsislav Varbanov in the new cabinet to be presented to parliament on Wednesday.
The agriculture ministry forecasts 1997 wheat output at some 3.0 million tonnes, up from last year's 1.8 million tonnes. Bulgaria's domestic consumption is estimated at some 1.6 million tonnes.
Excessive wheat exports two years ago and a bad harvest in 1996 created acute grain shortages earlier this year, which have been overcome in the past three months.
